title: Separate the first coincidence from the repeat period
chapter: Remainders turn long lists into short systems
goal: Find when two repeating events first coincide, and how often after that.

scenes.visual: Show two lights pulsing at separate rates above a shared timeline, with a marker for a first flash and for spacing.
scenes.narration: Two lights repeat at different speeds. One flashes every four seconds and the other every six. We can ask when they first flash together after starting. We can also ask how much time separates one meeting from the next.

scenes.visual: Lay down cards for four and six and trace valid step lengths along parallel rails.
scenes.narration: Twenty-four is a multiple of both four and six. A smaller common multiple may also work. First mark where each light starts. Then add its own period each time. A timeline shows both the starting positions and the repeated jumps.

scenes.visual: Draw both flashes at zero and leave future marks unfilled for the learner.
scenes.narration: Both lights flash at time zero. One repeats every four seconds. The other repeats every six seconds. When do they next flash together? List a few times for each light, and line up the lists.

scenes.visual: Progressively fill both time rows; join common flashes at twelve and twenty-four, then bracket the spacing.
scenes.narration: The first light flashes at four, eight, twelve and sixteen. The second flashes at six, twelve and eighteen. Their first positive meeting is at twelve seconds. Twelve is the lowest common multiple of four and six. A gap between meetings has to be a multiple of both periods, so the next meeting is twelve seconds later.

scenes.visual: Shift the six-second row two units right while keeping its marks equally spaced. Connect meetings at eight and twenty.
scenes.narration: Let the second light start at time two. Its times are two, eight, fourteen and twenty. The first light's times stay on the multiples of four. The first meeting moves to eight seconds, and the next is at twenty. The starting offset changed the first meeting. The twelve-second gap stayed the same.

scenes.visual: Shift the lower rail to offset one. Colour the even and odd columns and leave no vertical match.
scenes.narration: Now start the second light at time one. Its jumps of six keep all its times odd. Starting from zero and moving in jumps of four keeps the other times even. An odd time and an even time cannot match, so these two lights never flash together.

scenes.visual: Keep the two start markers and the spacing labels, then set up the bus departures notebook exercise.
scenes.narration: When meetings are possible, the lowest common multiple gives the gap between them. The starting positions decide when the first meeting happens. In your notebook, one bus leaves every eight minutes and another every twelve. They both leave at nine o'clock. When do they next leave together?

notebook_exercise: Buses leave every 8 minutes and every 12 minutes, both at 9:00. When do they next leave together?
notebook_answer: The lowest common multiple of 8 and 12 is 24, so at 9:24.
